results.title: How Students Use—and Hide—AI in Online Assessments and What ...
results.content: This targeted survey focused on students’ experiences with online assessments, use of AI tools, and related ethical concerns. To understand how students view the evolving role of AI tools in academic work, we asked them to respond to three broad policy statements in **Q8: AI Acceptable**: (1) AI is acceptable if used for support but not to generate full answers, (2) AI should not be allowed at all in graded assessments, and (3) AI use should be encouraged provided citation guidance is given. These findings, when viewed alongside the broader patterns of disclosure behaviour and ethical concerns explored earlier, point to important tensions and opportunities in how institutions might foster transparency, trust in student work, and constructive AI use through both policy and assessment design, a theme we now examine in the Discussion. This paper reports on a small-scale survey of undergraduate economics students, exploring their perceptions, behaviours, and ethical concerns around the use of AI tools in online assessments.
